title: App Entry & Bootstrap
description: The application bootstraps from src/main.ts, a 7-line entry point that imports the global stylesheet and mounts the root Svelte component to #app while injecting Vercel analytics. App.svelte is the ~4431-line monolithic root component orchestrating the entire UI—equipment slots, enchantment selection, weapon arts, drag-and-drop, and summary displays. app.css provides the design tokens (colors, spacing, shadows, typography) that every component consumes. This step gives you the big picture before diving into the engine.

title: Type System & Game Data
description: types.ts defines the central domain contracts—StatMap, BuildState, enchantments, weapon blades/handles, monk gloves/essences—and derives the stat-key taxonomy using keyof/typeof and template-literal types. It also exports small helpers like applyUpgrade (scaling stats by equipment level) and canProc (proc-coefficient check) used across the engine. engine/data.ts is the barrel re-exporting the typed data accessors built on these contracts. Understanding these types is essential before reading the calculation pipeline.

title: State Management (The Store)
description: store.ts is the single source of truth for the player build. It exposes a Svelte writable store with debounced localStorage persistence, a derived damage result, and mutation helpers (setEnchantment, setGuild, moveArmorSlot, swapEnchantments) that every UI flow calls. The derived result store is what powers every damage display in the app. setGuild even swaps weapons, gloves, and essences automatically when you switch to the Draconic or Monk guilds.

title: JSON Game Data & Lookup Functions
description: The engine/data/ directory loads and indexes game items from the JSON catalogs in src/data/—races, guilds, perks, armors, rings, runes, enchantments, blades, handles, gloves, and essences—exposing typed getters (getRace, getArmorPart, getEnchant, getBlade, getGlove). perks.json is the most depended-on file in the graph (fan-in 9), because every equipment catalog references its 247+ perk definitions. enchantments.json models 51 enchants split into unAscended/Ascended tiers with stacking rules and stat modifiers.

title: Weapon Calculation
description: weapon.ts resolves the final weapon type from blade+handle combinations (including perk overrides like Dual Wielding), merges part scalings and stats, detects hybrid weapons, and handles the monk glove/essence path with rank-based bonuses. shrine.ts applies tier-based shrine multipliers (tier 1 = 3x down to tier 5 = 1x) to both stats and scalings. The resulting WeaponResult feeds every downstream damage formula.

title: Enchantment System
description: enchant.ts applies enchantment modifiers to equipment slots in two phases—selector transforms first, then direct stat/perk modifiers—and enforces exclusive vs. stacked slot rules via enforceEnchantSlot. Infusion halves all stats while copying perks, and perk effectiveness scales by (1 + 0.1*stacks). _utils.ts supplies the round2/round4 helpers with epsilon compensation that keep every engine calculation numerically consistent.

title: Core Damage Calculation Engine
description: build.ts is the heart of the application: calcBuild() runs accumulateEquipment → finalizePerks → deriveResults to turn a BuildState into a full BuildResult. It orchestrates data lookup, enchantment application, shrine multipliers, cooldown reduction (calcCDR), boost multipliers (calcBoosts), buff assembly (computeBuffs), and damage-type bonuses. Its 21 outgoing edges make it the second-largest hub after BuffData.ts, tying the entire engine together.
languageLesson: build.ts is composed as a layered pipeline of pure functions (accumulateEquipment, finalizePerks, deriveResults) that are called sequentially, keeping each stage independently testable and reusable.

title: Constants, Buffs & Perk Definitions
description: constants/index.ts is the wildcard barrel aggregating every hardcoded game value—damage-type colors and priorities, crit thresholds, CDR, defensive values, draconic multipliers, and perk base damages. buffs.ts holds 160+ buff/debuff potency constants, while BuffData.ts (the highest fan-out node at 38 edges) assembles and modifies the active buff set from perks, potions, and weapon arts. statboost.ts applies stat-conversion perks (Weight Distribution, Quick Witted, Carapace) in a strict registry order.

title: UI Components & Shared Primitives
description: DamageAnalyzer.svelte is the largest component in the project (8k+ lines), managing build state and feeding BaseDamageCalc through an ~80-prop interface to compute per-hit and per-tick damage. BuffList renders the assembled active buff set, and WeaponStatsDisplay presents weapon stats as colored pills split into damage types, scalings, and boosts. Shared primitives like Badge, Button, and RollValue are the reusable building blocks every modal and panel relies on.

title: Build Saves, Controls & Polish
description: BuildSaves.svelte (~1360 lines) handles localStorage save slots, base64 import/export, fuzzy search, and drag-and-drop reordering. CdrStepsCalc visualizes each cooldown-reduction step as a chain, while EmotionalTracker and the other trackers expose game-specific toggles that write into the build store. StatFilter and WeaponStatFilter provide tri-state include/exclude filtering for the equipment modals, and AppHeader ties save management and the Overview/Analyze tabs together.

title: Documentation & Deployment
description: ONBOARDING.md is a complete architecture guide—layers, key concepts, and a guided tour—that confirms the structure you have just walked through. On the delivery side, vite.config.ts wires the Svelte build plus PWA/service-worker support, package.json defines the dev/build/check/test scripts, and vercel.json or the GitHub Pages workflow (static.yml) publish the static output. These stops show how the calculator goes from source to a deployed, installable web app.
languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows use 'on' triggers, 'jobs' for parallel work, and 'steps' for sequential commands; here a build job compiles the Vite app and uploads the dist artifact, then a deploy job publishes it to Pages.
